scope.flow: HypoVault performance-fee accounting via transferable shares and average cost basis
scope.environment: HypoVault contract with ERC20 transferable shares and userBasis accounting

statements.text: Alice holds a highly profitable position where market value exceeds her cost basis.
Bob holds a position at a loss with a high-cost basis.
Bob transfers his shares to Alice.

_transferBasis adds the incoming basis to the recipient's existing basis via userBasis[to] += basisToTransfer without distinguishing pre-existing profitable positions from the incoming position's financial history.
Alice's account receives a new artificially inflated average cost basis mixing the profitable and losing positions.
The inflated basis can be made equal to or greater than current market value, making calculated profit zero or negative and completely eliminating the performance fee on withdrawal.
Any two or more colluding users can systematically and completely evade performance fees, reducing protocol fee income to near zero if widely adopted.
A secondary market for loss trading is created where users with losing positions sell their high-cost basis to profitable users.
Performance fees should be calculated on genuine profit such that transferring shares cannot merge a losing position's high-cost basis into a profitable position to reduce or eliminate the fee.
Alice and Bob collude to execute the share transfer and subsequent withdrawal.

ambiguities: Report does not specify exact numeric values of basis, market value, or fee amounts.
Withdrawal step that realizes the zero/negative profit is described but not given as a distinct action.
Unfairness to regular holders (impact 3) and flawed economic model (impact 4) omitted as less directly observable.
